Same Test, Two Ceilings

2026-08-19 · exploratory · no prereg, no verdict

Test 04 run twice: once to 232, once to 248. Nothing else changes — same two independent series, same forty zeros, same transform. Only the amount of ladder each base gets. Within a column every axis is identical; the two columns differ because the taller ceiling reaches larger residuals.

The question this answers: does a feature belong to the base, or to how little ladder that base had? Octadic reads −0.766 at 232 on ten points and +0.714 at 248 on sixteen. Pentadic moves the other way, +0.707 to −0.354. Dyadic and triadic have enough rungs at either ceiling and both simply improve.

Hollow markers are depths computed from fewer than ten points; the count is printed above every marker. π from primecountpy, li of a complex argument as Ei(ρ log x), forty zeros from mpmath at 40 digits.
